name: Visual Explainer
summary: The voice tells a story and the screen builds it out of paper: cut-out photos, a blue highlighter shape, serif headlines, arrows and sourced stat cards snap in on stepped stop-motion as each word is spoken.
best_for: Educators, analysts, finance and history explainers, researchers, and brands explaining why something works. 45-90 second idea-led videos, with or without a face.
why_it_works: The hook is a question or surprising fact on a stacked headline in the first 2s, and the answer is withheld until the last 20%, so the open loop carries the whole video. Elements build onto the same plate every 1.5-2.5s, which feels like progress and rewards watching. Stepped stop-motion is a texture most feeds never show, which is itself a pattern interrupt. Short boxed-keyword captions (max 26 characters per line) keep reading effortless while the visuals do the teaching.

preview.caption_sample: The reason why is not what you think
preview.motion_sample: On warm paper, a cut-out photo with a white outline snaps in on stepped frames, a blue circle scales up behind it, a bold serif headline stamps in and a marker swipe highlights one word.
